body.statement: For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the finite structural chart enumeration of \(\mathscr A\) terminates using arithmetic and order tests over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). There is an explicit computable constant \(B_{k,\ell}\le 2^{2^{C(k\ell+k+\ell)}}\), for a universal constant \(C\), bounding the number of labeled charts and the algebraic degree over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). If every coordinate of \(\zeta\) is an explicitly encoded rational whose numerator and denominator have binary length at most \(L\), a Turing implementation terminates; after clearing denominators, every algebraic target certificate uses a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(B_{k,\ell}\) and rational isolating endpoints, and every coefficient and endpoint has bit length at most \(B_{k,\ell}(L+1)^C\). The classification is obtained from the structural charts in \(\mathscr A\), not by reporting generic two-copy quantifier elimination.
body.justification: The field-relative statement separates symbolic exactness for real data from bit complexity for rational encodings.
body.gap: Fixed-dimensional real algebraic decision is known, but no end-to-end field-relative certificate and rational-input size bound exists for this structural response-cycle compiler.
body.consumer: Symbolic implementations can certify real-parameter outputs, while exact-arithmetic implementations can validate rational-data certificates with explicit size bounds.

obligation.what_is_open: Termination, chart-count, algebraic-degree, and rational certificate-size bounds for the specific structural compiler.
obligation.obstruction: Without a complete mixed-support structural enumeration there is no finite list whose chart number, elimination degree, or coefficient growth can be bounded. A generic real-algebraic decision bound applies to the raw fiber but violates the theorem's stated method.
obligation.attempted: Counted the fixed-alphabet raw variables, constraints, and degrees, and verified termination of the completed rank-two and residual-forest branches.
obligation.partial_result: For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the normalized cycle equations contain finitely many real variables and finitely many polynomial equalities and inequalities.  After one redundant coordinate is removed from each simplex, their numbers are bounded by \(C_0(k\ell+k+\ell)\) for a universal constant \(C_0\), and their degrees are at most two before residual proportionality is eliminated.  The established all-rank-two branch terminates by enumerating at most \(2^4\) orientations and then performing finitely many linear-algebra and order tests over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The established residual-forest branch terminates by finitely many residual-zero, signed-ratio, forest-propagation, cycle-product, normalization, and relevance tests.  Generic real-algebraic decision and sampling applied to the raw fixed-alphabet fiber would yield a terminating doubly exponential envelope, but it would be the forbidden generic classifier rather than the stated structural compiler.  Because the mixed-support structural enumeration is not yet proved exhaustive, neither its chart count nor its algebraic-degree and rational bit-size bounds have been derived.
